title: FLEX: oxygen level where droplet flames start to go out

facts.method: 1. Logistic fit of P(test ends in extinction) on oxygen mole fraction. 2. Transition oxygen = where that probability is 50%; 95% interval from 2000 bootstrap resamples of the experiments. 3. Shuffle test: the oxygen-outcome link is re-fitted on 2000 random relabelings. 4. Later-date check: the transition is fitted on the earliest 80% of test dates and its predictions scored on the latest 20% (balanced accuracy vs always predicting extinction). A transition is reported only when the interval lies inside the tested oxygen range, the shuffle p-value is below 0.01 and the later-date check beats the baseline. Otherwise the result says no transition is supported.

title: SAME and SAME-R: smoke particles and the ISS smoke detector

facts.source: NASA PSI-101 (SAME-R) and PSI-102 (SAME), 'Combined SAMER Results' reduced data, sheet 'Reduced Data with ISS Det'
facts.method:
Reads backend/falmex/datasets/PSI-101_SAME_smoke_tests.csv (build_same_table.py) and tests
three questions, each in both flights separately, so the second flight is a replication:
  1 aging      does smoke held in the chamber grow? Paired: the same sample before and after
               secondary aging (test "23" vs "23a"); exact sign test.
  2 material   do materials make different particle sizes? Kruskal-Wallis on the count mean
               diameter of unaged smoke (aging under 120 s).
  3 detector   does the ISS smoke detector (light scattering) respond to particle size beyond
               the amount of smoke? Spearman partial correlation of detector signal with count
               mean diameter, holding the mass moment M1 fixed; 2000 shuffles.
DBP (dibutyl phthalate) is a calibration aerosol, not a fire fuel, and is left out.

title: Saffire-III: a real fire inside the Cygnus spacecraft

facts.source: NASA PSI-100 (Saffire-III), Saffire_Data_Table2017.161.00.42.03-EU.csv, Cygnus telemetry of 5 June 2017
facts.method:
Source: NASA PSI-100, "Saffire_Data_Table2017.161.00.42.03-EU.csv" (engineering units, Cygnus
flight of 5 June 2017). Cleaning: one row with a negative clock is dropped; radiometer values
of -1000 or less are "sensor off" sentinels and cabin channels that read exactly 0 are
missing values, both set empty. Time is RelativeSeconds / 1000.

Per ignited sample (igniter current above 0.5 A), with fixed rules:
  burn          a radiometer pair is "lit" while its mean is 10 units above its median of
                the 120 s before that sample's ignition; first/last lit time, peak and its time
  spread        the time between the peaks of the two radiometer pairs (the flame front passing
                one pair, then the other); no distance is given in the file, so no speed
  smoke         the first time the responding Cygnus scatter detector is 0.2 above its median
                of the 120 s before ignition for three samples in a row; peak and its time
  cabin         rise of pressure and temperature (max in the window minus the pre-ignition median)
Each sample's window runs from its ignition to the next sample's ignition (at most 15 min),
so one burn is never credited to another.

title: Saffire-I and II: which samples burned (11 samples)

facts.source: NASA PSI-98 (Saffire-I) and PSI-99 (Saffire-II) per-sample sensor workbooks, sheet 'Calibrated Data'
facts.method:
Source: NASA PSI-98 "Saffire-I Sample <k> Sensor Data Complete TM graphs.xlsx" (k = 1, 2)
and PSI-99 "Saffire Sensor Data Sample <k>.xlsx" (k = 1..9), both flown on Cygnus cargo
craft, sheet "Calibrated Data" (about 30 readings per second; dates from its clock). Nothing is
modelled. Per sample, with fixed rules:
  conditions  median of the 30 s before the igniter came on: oxygen and CO2 (%), pressure
              (psia), air speed (mean of the two anemometers, cm/s), humidity, inlet air
  igniter     on = igniter current above 0.5 A; when it came on and for how long
  burned      a sample thermocouple (TC7-TC12, on the sample) stays more than 100 °C above
              its pre-ignition median for at least 5 s, counted only from 2 s after the
              igniter switched off (the hot igniter wire heats nearby thermocouples itself)
  flame       per responding thermocouple: peak rise and its time after ignition; how long
              the sample stayed hot (> 100 °C rise) after the igniter switched off; the time
              between the first and the last thermocouple peak (the flame front passing
              along the sample; no positions are given, so no speed)
  box         oxygen and CO2 change: median of the record's last 30 s minus the
              pre-ignition median, with the sensor's noise (half the 5-95% spread before
              ignition; the oxygen sensor steps by ~0.2% with no flame, so smaller changes
              are not readable); pressure rise (highest reading after ignition minus the
              median); the hottest plume thermocouple (TC1-TC6, downstream air)
  radiometers peak rise above the pre-ignition median; the igniter alone raises some
              radiometers by up to ~30 units, so they are not used to decide "burned"
facts.note: The workbooks name samples by number only; materials are not given in them, so none are claimed here.

title: FLEX-2: every raw test log summarised

facts.source: NASA PSI-68 (FLEX-2), per-test main logs and MDCA test-point settings
facts.method:
Reads, for each test point, NASA's main log "<TEST>.txt" (sequence timestamps and a 1 Hz table
of the narrow- and wide-view radiometers with chamber pressure and temperature) and
"<TEST>_MDCA_Testpoint_Settings.txt" (commanded settings). Nothing is modelled. Per test:
  sequence    date, igniter on time and power, the burn-to-completion window
  setup       fiber-supported or free droplet, which fuel dispenser, soot sampler used
  flame       wide-view radiometer (the narrow one saturates); baseline = median of the
              readings before the igniter came on; "lit" = 1 Hz readings above 20% of the
              peak (the slow decay of hot gas afterwards is not counted). The hot igniter
              wire itself glows, so a flame is "seen" only when the radiometer stays lit for
              at least 2 s starting 1 s after the igniter switched off; flame seconds =
              lit readings; first flame = first lit reading
  chamber     median pressure (psia) and temperature (°C); their rise during the test
The atmosphere (oxygen, diluent) is logged in the larger per-test chamber files, not read
here, so it is not in this table.

title: What FlamexSI cannot claim
facts: No partial-gravity (Moon, Mars) combustion data exists in PSI yet; microgravity and 1 g results only bound those cases.
Findings are statistical associations, not causes, and are not yet signed off by a combustion expert (evidence readiness level 7 is never automatic).
Droplet results (FLEX) are not cabin fires; the radiometers in Saffire sit next to the sample, unlike cabin sensors.
FLEX-2 oxygen and diluent per test are not in the public files: the per-test chamber logs (checked, 686 of 690 downloadable) hold only pressure and temperature.
